question: How is food stored in brown algae?

options.text: In the form of complex carbohydrates that may be in the form of laminarin or mannitol
In the form of complex lipids
In the form of oil droplets

solution:
The correct answer is __**In the form of complex carbohydrates that may be in the form of laminarin or mannitol**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Food is stored in brown algae in the form of complex carbohydrates that may be in the form of laminarin or mannitol.

 
 
• **Algae **are a type of organism that **bears chlorophyll and have a basic thalloid-like structure** and consume food in an **autotrophic manner**.
 
• **Aquatic creatures** that can exist in both **freshwater and saltwater environments include algae**.
 
• The three primary classes of algae are **Chlorophyceae, Phaeophyceae, and Rhodophyceae**.
 
 
 
• **Phaeophyceae**
 
 
• The Phaeophyceae family includes **brown algae**.
 
• They are mostly found in** habitats that are marine**.
 
• **Complex carbohydrates, such as laminarin or mannitol, are stored in the form of food**.
 
• A few examples are **Ectocarpus, Dictyota, Laminaria, Sargassum, and Fucus**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
